solutions.check: 32 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 31 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Twist a Shylock ? Say, what a beast!

parts.note: a twist or kink is a sharp bend in a line

indicators.note: the question 'Say' tells the solver to go by how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Shylock is the Jewish moneylender in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in horror at the sight of a contorted Shylock.
explanation.walkthrough: This 1960s clue leans on a stereotype that would not pass now. 'Say' marks a sound-alike: JOU, as in the French pronunciation, sounds like the word for Shylock's faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The kinkajou is a tree-dwelling mammal of Central and South America, so it is certainly a beast.

clue.text: With which to " cross " the palm of Beethoven's violinist?

definitions.text: With which to " cross " the palm
definitions.meaning: the old silver coin of South Germany and Austria, whose name comes from the cross stamped on it, the coin you would give a fortune-teller
Rodolphe ..., the French violinist to whom Beethoven dedicated his Violin Sonata No. 9

explanation.walkthrough: Kreuz is German for cross, which is why 'cross' sits in quotation marks: the coin is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a small old coin bearing a cross, fit for crossing a fortune-teller's palm, and the dedicatee of Beethoven's famous sonata.

clue.text: European winner has a go, anyhow

indicators.note: done anyhow means in a careless jumbled way, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Continental victor takes a turn, in no particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is only a link word; 'anyhow' scrambles WINNER, A and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Norway is a native of a country on the European continent.

clue.text: Pupil's present to teacher ?

parts.note: the traditional fruit a schoolchild leaves on the teacher's desk, especially in American lore

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' might suggest the eye, but this is the schoolchild's gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing a shiny red fruit to the teacher is the classic gesture of a well-behaved schoolchild.

clue.text: To get rich let up on mismanagement

indicators.note: mismanaged letters are badly handled and so end up in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone prospers by easing off on poor running of a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get' is a link; 'mismanagement' rearranges LET, UP and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes great wealth and luxurious display.

clue.text: Fiery lampoons

parts.note: short satirical attacks that share their name with small spluttering fireworks

explanation.definitionFit: A squib is a short sharp satire, and also a small hissing firework, hence fiery.

clue.text: Comical as a monocled question-master?

parts.note: odd or amusing, and also like one who sets a quiz while peering through a quizzing-glass, an old monocle

explanation.definitionFit: Quizzical means oddly amusing or questioning, and a quizzing-glass was a single eyeglass, so a monocled quizmaster fits both.

clue.text: Trader's perfect definition of his job

parts.note: the trader describing his work speaks in the first person, I
a trader's business is to deal, to buy and sell

explanation.surface: A merchant gives a flawless account of what his work involves.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the trader's description of his work aloud as 'I deal'; 'perfect' sits between the pieces as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Time's up about half-time ? Swift work!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
in a down clue, going up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time; with the 's it gives ERAS

indicators.note: half of the word that follows is kept, its first two letters only

explanation.surface: A sports commentator notes the clock has run out around the interval, calling it quick play.
explanation.walkthrough: ERAS turned 'up' gives SARE, which goes 'about' TI. Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal, famous works of mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift is the great Irish satirist, so his writing is the classic example of the genre of ridicule.

clue.text: Falstaff's most forcible recruit, though weak

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2 Falstaff calls the women's tailor he recruits 'most forcible ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Francis Feeble is the recruit Falstaff jokingly praises as 'most forcible', and the word itself means lacking strength.

clue.text: Send parent to wander by the river

indicators.note: letters sent to wander stray from their places and end up in a new order

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone sends a mother or father off to roam beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wander' rearranges PARENT into ENRAPT; 'by the' is a link, and the river supplies URE.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone, in the slang sense, is to thrill or delight them utterly.

clue.text: Vichy man suffers a loss, uncommonly foolish

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
this man losing something means a letter, here the separate word a, is taken out of his name

parts.note: Marshal Pétain headed the Vichy government of wartime France

explanation.surface: A wartime French collaborator suffers a defeat and seems remarkably stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: PETAIN 'suffers a loss' of the clue's A, leaving PETIN, which 'uncommonly' rearranges. The grid prints INERT, but its fourth square is unchecked and the wordplay gives INEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and lacking good sense, a close synonym of silly.

clue.text: The Maine subject

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A heading about the state of Maine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is taken as written; it reads like part of a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic a piece of writing or speech is about.

clue.text: One no good as a trustee, being comparatively Welsh?

definitions.text: One no good as a trustee, being comparatively Welsh?

parts.words: One no good as a trustee, being comparatively Welsh?
parts.note: someone who steals money placed in their care, and whose name sounds like 'more inclined to welsh', that is to dodge paying what is owed

explanation.walkthrough: Welsh here is the verb, to cheat by not paying a debt, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who misappropriates funds entrusted to them is the opposite of a reliable trustee, and to welsh is to fail to pay up.

clue.text: East Side toff demanding immediate action

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
a toff is British slang for a posh well-dressed man, a gent

explanation.surface: A smart gentleman from Manhattan's East Side wants things done at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Side' looks like the New York district, but it splits into E and XI, a team of eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: An exigent situation is pressing or urgent, requiring action now.

clue.text: See about row bird raised with The Avengers

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the others

parts.note: taken as written, the word see
a row is a din, a loud noise
the emu is the flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Someone watches a noisy bird being lifted alongside a television spy team.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE goes 'about' DIN and EMU to give SEDINEMUE, and 'raised' turns the lot. The Eumenides are the Furies of Greek myth, spirits of vengeance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies were avenging goddesses, euphemistically called the kindly ones, who punished wrongdoers.

clue.text: Put in secret form in French ethic

parts.note: en is French for in
an ethic is a moral code

explanation.surface: Someone renders a French moral principle into cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French' looks like part of the definition but gives EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To encode a message is to convert it into cipher.

clue.text: Doctor eager to have one article from man in India

parts.note: avid means keen or eager
the Roman numeral I is one
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A keen physician wants a single item from an Indian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' and 'from' are link words; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dravidians are the peoples of southern India speaking Tamil, Telugu and related languages.

clue.text: Inform against stupid fellow holding one up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a dunce is a slow-witted person

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone betrays a dim-witted man who is delaying a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ONE into ENO, which DUNCE is 'holding'.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to accuse them publicly or report them to the authorities.

clue.text: Maxims of financial power ?

definitions.meaning: the ... of Zurich, a jibe at Swiss bankers' power over currencies

explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a pithy saying, and 'the gnomes of Zurich' was a 1960s jibe at the Swiss bankers who moved currency markets.

clue.text: Daddy's so sweet?

parts.note: a rich older man who lavishes gifts on a young partner is a sugar daddy, so such a daddy is sweet in that way

explanation.definitionFit: Sugary means very sweet, and a sugar daddy is a generous older lover.

clue.text: The translation of St Jerome

parts.note: the fourth-century Latin version of the Bible made by Jerome, used by the Catholic Church

explanation.definitionFit: Jerome's Latin Bible became the standard Roman Catholic text and is known by that name.

clue.text: Food factor with sort of rating one found in French wine

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: vin is French for wine
TAM was the British Television Audience Measurement system of TV ratings
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A nutrient with a certain score is discovered in a bottle of French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. TAM ratings were the 1950s and 60s British television audience figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamins were once called accessory food factors, nutrients needed in small amounts.

clue.text: Provide dyke-maker with lift on the road

indicators.note: in a down clue, a lift raises the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: King Offa of Mercia built Offa's Dyke, the earthwork along the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: Someone gives a ditch-digger a ride in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa's Dyke is an eighth-century earthwork along the Welsh border. 'lift' raises the king's name in this down clue, and 'with' and 'on the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to supply or yield, as a window affords a view.

clue.text: Battled with, say, Galahad for a half-moon

indicators.note: say tells the solver that the words are to be judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: to battle with someone is to have fought them
Sir Galahad was the purest knight of the Round Table, and 'say' covers him too: knight is pronounced like the dark hours, its K silent

explanation.surface: Someone battled with Sir Galahad for half a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' governs both pieces: in a British accent, without the R, 'fought knight' sounds like the answer. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of fourteen days is roughly half a lunar month, the time between full and new moon.

clue.text: Lawyers turn up at African port

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reverses the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers arrive at a harbour in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' looks like 'arrive', but it reverses BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital of Morocco, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Money for an African charger

definitions.meaning: a large horned animal of Africa that charges at threats

explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is dated British slang for cash, and the rhinoceros is the hefty horned African beast famous for charging.

clue.text: But it would be a bit of a step down too

definitions.text: But it would be a bit of a step down too

parts.words: But it would be a bit of a step down too
parts.note: the vertical part of a stair, which you pass going down as well as up, despite a name suggesting only ascent

explanation.definitionFit: The upright board between treads in a staircase is part of each step whether you climb or descend.

clue.text: Is "this sceptred isle " so round too?

definitions.text: Is "this sceptred isle " so round too?

parts.words: Is "this sceptred isle " so round too?
parts.note: the monarch carries a sceptre and an orb, so a land described as having a sceptre might also be said to have a globe, meaning round

explanation.definitionFit: Orbed means shaped like a sphere, and the orb accompanies the sceptre in the regalia, as Gaunt's 'sceptred isle' speech evokes.

clue.text: Forgiveness for being careless with a charged particle

parts.note: remiss means negligent or careless
an ion is an atom or molecule with an electric charge

explanation.surface: Being pardoned for negligence with an electrically charged particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for being' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is pardon, as in the remission of sins.

clue.text: Experience hate of French exam

parts.note: de is French for of
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a French examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Experience' joins 'hate' in the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to feel intense loathing.

clue.text: Violate one point — and bang!

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
N, north, is a point of the compass
a bang is the American word for a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead

explanation.surface: Breaking a rule on a single point, then an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bang' looks like a noise but is a fringe of hair; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a law or right is to break or encroach on it.
